items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: me and George would play along with him... George again on banjo... Me and Joy, and, and, and, uh, George, and, uh, George Foster... with band

ctx.x: In other words, you help each other out. That's what the idea is.

You see, that's, that's where Joy and Lou's band had such a good reputation, good name, you see? Anytime when, uh, Kid Howard was playing at a, at a solo, me and George would play along with him, you understand? Every, anytime George had a solo, me and Howard would play along with George. And every time I had a solo, they'd play along with me. And after we, you think, we'd turn the rhythm loose, you see? You know? They'd play one or two chords, then we'd all come on in together, you understand? Music, all goes…
So you'd kind of swap the lead around, huh? It's easy idea, and then everybody would keep working. I'd get the picture of them.

items.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan…
items.q: People like Jim Robinson, George Lewis, Kit Howard, I mean...

ctx.x: How did you get hold of these men in the first place? Did they find out about you?
Well, these men are, you know, live here. Yeah. And a lot of them are quite famous. People like Jim Robinson, George Lewis, Kit Howard, I mean...
Excuse me for interrupting you here, Alan, but you said George Lewis. Now Lewis has just returned from Europe. How do you get him to come back here and play a one-night or a two-night stand?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: going across the front of the stage was George Lewis, uh... Kid Howard, and Jim Robinson.

ctx.x: Well, I wouldn't, I wouldn't count on that either because, you know, he might not remember. I know I talked to Chris Kelly's wife about when he died, and what she said was when he was hot at the time. He couldn't remember. Did you pray in Buddy Catee's? Did he have, for the funeral? Did you pray for the funeral?

They were, he's funeral gave for Chris Kelly's funeral. Uh, Buddy had two bands. He had the Eureka band. And I got a pickup, get together band. And, uh, Chris Kelly had two bands. And, uh, Chris Kelly had two bands. And, uh, uh, he got a popper. And, uh, uh, he got a popper. And, uh, uh, he got a popper. And, uh, I just thought it was popper too. Uh, Buddy came in for a couple of Chris's. Uh, Chris was right out the country. Uh, you know, he started playing. He started a band down in the country. All them out of,…
It might have been out there, but I'm just wondering, it's very hard to establish. Well, think of this in relation to when you played with Ivan Thomas when he was murdered. That was 30.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-12
items.q: So, I guess that means people like Jim Robinson would have... it would have hurt them to a certain extent. Being trombone players at that time, it would have been better to have been a trumpet player, or, I mean, more work than a trumpet player, or... I should imagine.

ctx.x: So, okay, can you remember the time when you were playing with Ivan Thomas, when he was murdered? Yeah, sure. Can you tell us something about that? One thing I'd like to know is, can you remember any of the other people in the band? Yeah. Pomp. Pomp. Changer. Bruce Robinson, the piano. Walter Preston playing banjo. Chani on the drum. Steve Antonis. Uh-huh. And a young footballer named Al was playing tennis. Uh-huh. Those old boys were in that band at that time. He didn't have a bass player? No, he was using two…

School. I have a kid. Nick's symphony. His father had a grocery store. About stuff like stuff That's how I got to find it with Nick. He liked it so much, so... He liked to run a business, and he really runs a business really good. I'd better complain about Nick, but he still runs my business, right? He does not? He's alright. I mean, he's not in music. No, he's alive. He's alive. Yeah. Um, can you remember how long he was your manager, and when Dorothy Tate took over? Can you remember, I've never been able to…
